plugins.name: PlanX GeoStats Lab
plugins.description: PlanX spatial analysis lab for QGIS planning workflows: data preparation, urban pattern scanning, hot spots, centers, exploratory models and scenarios, and machine learning and explainable AI.
plugins.about: PlanX GeoStats Lab brings advanced spatial statistics and machine learning tools to the QGIS Processing Toolbox with a planning-analysis workflow designed for PlanX: Setup and Diagnostics, Data Preparation and Neighborhoods, Urban Pattern Scan, Hot Spots and Spatial Outliers, Centers Direction and Dispersion, Models and Scenarios, and Machine Learning and Explainable AI. The model workflow includes OLS, Generalized Linear Regression, Spatial Lag Regression, Spatial Error Regression, Spatial Durbin, Spatial Regime Regression, Exploratory Regression, Quantile Regression, GWR, MGWR, Eigenvector Spatial Filtering, model comparison and sensitivity testing. The Machine Learning group adds Random Forest, Extra Trees, Gradient Boosting (scikit-learn/XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost), SVM, Neural Network, and TabPFN (2025 tabular foundation model) regression/classification; spatial k-fold cross-validation (K-Means block or kNNDM); and explainability tools including SHAP (global/spatial map/local), the exact-contribution Explainable Boosting Machine, DiCE counterfactual explanations, and distribution-free Conformal Prediction Intervals. Optional GeoStats Python libraries are managed only through Processing Toolbox tools under 00 | Setup and Diagnostics: GeoStats Library Status for non-installing diagnostics and Install / Update GeoStats Libraries for explicit, user-approved pip installation. Developed with feedback from educational workflows at Dokuz Eylul University, Department of City and Regional Planning. Online User Manual & Documentation: https://yusufeminoglu.github.io/planx_geostats/GEOSTATS_REFERENCE_MANUAL.html | If you find this plugin helpful, please consider starring the repository on GitHub (https://github.com/YusufEminoglu/planx_geostats)!

plugins.name: Linderos360CO
plugins.description: Generador de descripciones de linderos, plano cartográfico y tablas de coordenadas para los procesos catastrales colombianos (normativa del IGAC-SNR).
plugins.about:
Si trabajas en catastro o topografía en Colombia y tienes que generar
descripciones técnicas de linderos, ya sabes lo que implica: revisar la norma,
calcular coordenadas, armar el texto, hacer el plano... todo a mano o con
flujos poco automatizados.

Linderos360CO hace ese proceso completo desde QGIS. Seleccionas los predios,
configuras los campos de tu capa y el complemento genera los tres productos
que exige el flujo catastral:

- Descripción técnica de linderos (.txt): texto normativo con inicio en
vértice noroccidental, recorrido en sentido horario, segmentos agrupados
por cuadrante (Norte / Este / Sur / Oeste), identificación de colindantes
y área en hectáreas (rural) o m² (urbano). Todo según la resolución
conjunta IGAC-SNR de catastro multipropósito.

- Plano cartográfico (.pdf): generado desde una plantilla .qpt con escala
automática, mapa de localización OSM, leyenda dinámica y datos del
encabezado configurables (empresa, título, elaborado por, logo).

- Tabla de coordenadas (.xlsx): vértices con coordenadas proyectadas
MAGNA-SIRGAS / EPSG:9377, coordenadas geográficas WGS84, distancia y
azimut al siguiente vértice, y fila de totales con el perímetro.

El complemento trabaja en EPSG:9377 internamente sin importar el CRS de
tu capa fuente. Funciona con SHP, GPKG, GDB y cualquier formato vectorial
que soporte QGIS. También maneja capas con geometría MultiPolygonZ, que
es lo que suelen entregar las entidades catastrales colombianas.

REQUISITO ADICIONAL:
Para generar el archivo .xlsx necesitas tener instalado openpyxl. Si no
lo tienes, ejecuta esto en la consola Python de QGIS:
import subprocess; subprocess.run(['pip', 'install', 'openpyxl', '--break-system-packages'])

It provides 8 functional tabs covering: Geoprocessing (buffer, intersection, union, difference, convex hull), Joins (spatial, attribute CSV), Cleaning (invalid geometries, duplicates, simplify, repair), Calculations (area, perimeter, length, centroid, XY), Statistics (by category, points in polygons, aggregation), Processing (reproject, merge, clip, filter, convert), Export (CSV, Excel, GeoPackage, Shapefile), and Automation (field update, change detection). plugins.name: River Slope Calculator
plugins.description: Calculate river reach slope from a DEM using Average Slope or Equal Area Slope. Output unit selectable: m/m or %.
plugins.about:
River Slope Calculator computes the slope of each river reach feature (line or multiline) from an underlying DEM raster, supporting two methods:

1. Average Slope (Mean Gradient) — The absolute elevation difference between reach endpoints divided by the total reach length. The simplest and most commonly used slope measure.

2. Equal Area Slope — The slope of a line through the outlet that creates equal areas above and below the longitudinal elevation profile. Adopted in Australian Rainfall and Runoff (ARR, 1987) for the Bransby Williams time-of-concentration formula. Reference: Ladson (2017), NZ Ministry of Works (1980).

Both methods compute slope internally as dimensionless values (m/m). A new Output unit option lets you choose between m/m (dimensionless) and % (percent) — the result is multiplied by 100 when percent is selected. Slope values are added as new fields on a copy of the input reach layer. DEM elevation is sampled at a user-defined interval along each reach using trapezoidal integration for the Equal Area Slope.

plugins.name: Fishnet Creator
plugins.description: Create fishnet polygon/polyline grids equivalent to ArcGIS Create Fishnet. Pixel-perfect raster alignment, unit selector, rotation support, clip to boundary, label points, and temporary layer support.
plugins.about:
Fishnet Creator replicates the ArcGIS "Create Fishnet" workflow directly inside QGIS.

HOW TO USE:
1. Set your output path (or leave blank for a temporary scratch layer)
2. Define the grid extent — use a layer, canvas, or type coordinates manually
3. Set Origin and Y-Axis coordinates (Y-Axis controls rotation angle)
4. Enter Cell Width and Height, or Rows and Columns (auto-syncs Opposite Corner)
5. Choose CRS, geometry type, and optionally create label points
6. Click OK — the fishnet is generated and loaded into your map

KEY FEATURES:
- Exact ArcGIS Create Fishnet UI layout (Origin, Y-Axis, Cell Size, Rows/Cols, Opposite Corner)
- Grid rotation via Y-Axis coordinate
- Pixel-perfect raster alignment using GDAL geotransform
- Cell size unit selector: metres, km, feet, miles, yards, nautical miles, degrees
- Live coverage feedback showing total rows × columns
- Clip output to any polygon layer boundary
- Optional centroid label points layer
- Polygon or Polyline geometry output
- Temporary scratch layer mode (no file required)
- Compatible with QGIS 3.x and 4.x

REQUIREMENTS:
- QGIS 3.0 or higher (including QGIS 4.x)
- No extra Python libraries required

plugins.author: Cyanide

plugins.name: LiDAR Relief Visualization
plugins.description: A free, open-source QGIS toolkit with 31 Processing algorithms for archaeological LiDAR visualization and terrain analysis. Reveal subtle earthworks, prepare point clouds, compare surveys, combine LiDAR with satellite imagery, validate anomalies in the field, and produce reproducible research outputs.
plugins.about:
LiDAR Relief Visualization is a free and open-source archaeological terrain-analysis toolkit for QGIS and part of the Dig:Tools ecosystem.
Its 31 Processing algorithms help archaeologists, heritage professionals, and landscape researchers examine digital elevation models and LiDAR point clouds for subtle features such as ditches, banks, mounds, hollow ways, scarps, platforms, quarrying, and disturbed ground.
Core tools include multi-directional hillshade, SLRM, Sky-View Factor, anisotropic Sky-View Factor, positive and negative openness, Local Dominance, MSTP, e4MSTP, Terrain Ruggedness Index, slope, VAT, Simple Red Relief, PCA composites, visualization blending, and batch processing with landscape presets.
Extended workflows support LAS/LAZ ground filtering, PDAL processing, multi-temporal DEM comparison, LiDAR and Sentinel-2 fusion, Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF export, interactive web maps, QField survey packages, reproducible visualization recipes, PDF reporting, and optional ONNX-based feature detection.
Core terrain tools work with libraries supplied by QGIS. Specialized capabilities use clearly identified optional packages and remain isolated, so missing optional dependencies do not prevent the plugin from loading.
The plugin supports QGIS 3 and QGIS 4 and is tested through automated numerical, packaging, clean-runtime, and desktop-loader checks. It supports transparent, reproducible research without subscription fees or proprietary lock-in.
Visualizations and automated detections are interpretive aids rather than archaeological classifications. Assess potential features using complementary evidence and, where appropriate, field validation.
New to the plugin? Run "Visualisation Contact Sheet" to compare techniques on your own DEM in seconds, then open any algorithm and press Help for the full user guide. The guide also ships inside the plugin folder as USER_GUIDE.md, and is online at https://github.com/dig-tools/lidar-relief-qgis-plugin/blob/main/lidar_relief/USER_GUIDE.md
plugins.author: Mark Bouck

plugins.name: SIGMAI
plugins.description: Secure local AI-QGIS interface with auditable commands.
plugins.about: SIGMAI is a secure local bridge between AI agents and QGIS. It exposes validated JSON commands, bearer-token authentication, session discovery, permissions, dry-run support where applicable, audit logs, cartographic map generation, layer/project inspection, vector/raster tools, workflow foundations and plugin diagnostics. The bridge is local-only and binds to 127.0.0.1. Normal mode does not expose unrestricted Python execution. Developer Mode is explicit, warning-protected, disabled by default and intended for QGIS plugin development. SIGMAI is designed to use the Python and libraries bundled with QGIS/OSGeo4W; optional workflows may require QGIS Processing providers or user-installed plugins. Developed by Luan da Silva Cortes Maciel (MACIEL, L. S. C.) as a research product associated with Herpeto Mantiqueira.
plugins.author: MACIEL, L. S. C.

plugins.name: CityStockID Automated Urban Diagnostic AUD
plugins.description:
CityStockID Automated Urban Diagnostic AUD is a QGIS plugin designed to generate automated urban diagnostics from temporally harmonized gridded building stock data for Indonesia.

The plugin analyzes WorldPop and Google Open Buildings temporal building stock data at 100 m resolution to identify building growth, footprint expansion, vertical or mass densification, compact intensification, urban shrinking indication, morphological pressure, urban fringe dynamics, and preliminary spatial planning policy directions.

CityStockID supports evidence based urban and regional planning by transforming multi year building stock rasters into interpretable spatial indicators, zonal diagnostics, visual analytics, and automated HTML reporting.

The tool supports a wide range of planning applications including:
1. Urban growth and expansion monitoring
2. Building intensity and morphological pressure assessment
3. KDB, KLB, and KDH proxy screening
4. Urban shrinking indication and regeneration diagnostics
5. Compact growth and densification evaluation
6. Urban fringe and sprawl risk monitoring
7. RDTR and spatial planning policy support
8. Infrastructure capacity pressure screening
9. Strategic urban diagnostic reporting
plugins.about:
CityStockID provides an integrated automated urban diagnostic framework for analyzing Indonesia specific building stock dynamics using temporally harmonized gridded raster data.

The plugin combines remote sensing based building stock information, raster change analysis, zonal statistics, spatial morphology indicators, urban intensity proxies, and rule based planning diagnostics to support urban and regional planning decisions.

It generates key diagnostic indicators such as building stock change, percent growth, CAGR, KDB proxy, KLB proxy, KDH pressure, vertical intensity, average footprint size, perimeter surface ratio, compactness proxy, sprawl risk index, densification score, morphological pressure index, and urban intensity index.

CityStockID also classifies zonal urban dynamics into categories such as Urban Shrinking Indication, Growth Hotspot, Compact Intensification, Footprint Expansion, Vertical or Mass Densification, Moderate Growth, Stable or Low Change, Decline or Noise Candidate, and No Data.

The plugin produces preliminary policy directions through a 9 class classifier including Urban Shrinking Regeneration Direction, Sprawl Control, FAR Audit and Vertical Transition, Green or Open Space Priority and Overbuilt Control, Intensity and Infrastructure Capacity Audit, Anticipate Intensification and Guide Compact Growth, Footprint Expansion Monitoring, Stable or Low Change Area, and General Monitoring.

Outputs include a spatial diagnostic layer, raster summaries, zonal summary tables, optional XLSX workbook, modern PNG visualizations, and an automated HTML diagnostic report with planning conclusions.

CityStockID is designed for research, planning practice, spatial monitoring, RDTR support, urban growth assessment, and evidence based policy diagnostics in Indonesian urban and regional planning contexts.
plugins.author: Firman Afrianto, Maya Safira

plugins.name: Mapupdate360

plugins.about: Mapupdate360 helps QGIS users create photo point layers from geotagged 360 images, visualize local equirectangular imagery, navigate image sequences, view live map direction/frustum, enhance image display, apply panorama heading/orientation metadata, correct GPS-based camera mount offset, and create privacy-safe copies with camera-bottom blur/cover masking. This plugin is derived from the original Equirectangular Viewer plugin by Francisco Raga / All4GIS, with substantial enhancements by Pankaj Singh Kalam for 360-image-based 2D GIS map updating workflows.

plugins.name: PlanX CartoLab
plugins.description: Design publication-quality thematic maps and print layouts in QGIS: choropleths, bivariate maps, cartograms, ridge maps, dot-density, proportional symbols and hexbins; native 2.5D building styling; one-click map layouts with legend, scale bar and north arrow; and colorblind-safe color palettes.
plugins.about: PlanX CartoLab is a thematic mapping and print-layout studio for QGIS. It builds publication-ready choropleths (including bivariate and Value-by-Alpha), continuous-area cartograms, ridge-line relief maps, dot-density and Flannery proportional-symbol maps, hexbin aggregation, coordinate graticules and native 2.5D building styling - then assembles a complete print layout (map, legend, scale bar, north arrow, coordinate grid and credits) in one click. Includes adaptive classification (Geometric Interval, Fisher-Jenks, Head/Tail Breaks), choropleth normalization and rates, visual-center label points, and a Layout Manager to duplicate and export layouts to PNG/PDF. No external dependencies - pure QGIS. Online User Manual & Documentation: https://yusufeminoglu.github.io/planx_cartolab/ | If you find this plugin helpful, please consider starring the repository on GitHub (https://github.com/YusufEminoglu/planx_cartolab)!
plugins.author: Yusuf Eminoglu

plugins.name: PlanX DataCube Lab
plugins.description: Next-generation spatiotemporal analysis engine: data cubes, Emerging Hot Spot Analysis, time-series forecasting, and volumetric voxel rendering for QGIS.
plugins.about: PlanX DataCube Lab brings space-time cube analytics to QGIS by integrating xarray/Dask multi-dimensional array processing into a unified Processing framework. Build (X×Y×T×V) data cubes from vector or raster time series, run Emerging Hot Spot Analysis (EHSA) with 17 spatiotemporal pattern classifications, forecast future values via integrated ARIMA and Random Forest models, and render 3D volumetric voxel layers in QGIS 4 native engine. Online User Manual & Documentation: https://yusufeminoglu.github.io/planx_datacube/ | If you find this plugin helpful, please consider starring the repository on GitHub (https://github.com/YusufEminoglu/planx_datacube)!
plugins.author: Yusuf Eminoglu

plugins.name: KoboToolbox FieldBridge
plugins.description: Import KoboToolbox and ODK Central field survey data as QGIS vector layers. Supports geopoint, geotrace and geoshape. Incremental sync and auto-refresh included.
plugins.about: FieldBridge connects QGIS directly to KoboToolbox (API v2) and ODK Central (REST API) to import field survey submissions as vector layers. Supports all GPS field types: geopoint (Point), geotrace (LineString), geoshape (Polygon). Features include date range filtering, incremental sync (only new submissions since last import), auto-refresh timer, and a log console. No external Python dependencies required — built entirely on urllib and QGIS core. Designed for field data workflows in West Africa and beyond.
plugins.author: LOMPO Ibrahim

plugins.name: SoilTool
plugins.description: Interactive soil profile visualization tool for QGIS.
plugins.about: Scientific tool for visualising and managing soil profiles directly in QGIS vector layers. It allows adding horizons with custom properties like texture, color, and boundaries. No external Python libraries required.
plugins.author: Felipe Flores

plugins.name: House Numbering
plugins.description: A plugin for numbering house with dockable panels, update checker, and about dialog.
plugins.about:
This is a plugin that demonstrates the structure and best practices for QGIS plugin development.

Features:
- Dockable panels that can be positioned anywhere in the QGIS interface
- Plugin update checker that fetches the latest version from GitHub
- About dialog with version information
- Menu and toolbar integration
- One-click dependency installer using uv for fast cross-platform package management
- Isolated virtual environment for Python dependencies
- Clean, modular code structure following QGIS plugin guidelines

Requirements:
- Python packages: geopandas (installed automatically via Settings > Dependencies)

Use this template as a starting point for your own QGIS plugins.
plugins.author: ChienPham

plugins.name: geeSWAT
plugins.description: geeSWAT is a QGIS plugin that integrates Google Earth Engine to support SWAT hydrological modelling workflows.
plugins.about:
geeSWAT is a QGIS plugin that integrates Google Earth Engine to support
SWAT (Soil and Water Assessment Tool) hydrological modelling workflows.

Connects QGIS with GEE to download and preprocess spatial data required
for hydrological basin delineation and SWAT model setup.
plugins.author: Geomatica Ambiental

plugins.name: Numerar Ruta
plugins.description: Sequentially numbers points along a route line based on spatial order.
plugins.about: Tool that opens a modal dialog to sequentially number points that fall on a route line, in the order defined by the line's geometry from start to end. Points at the same location share the same number, and junction points between consecutive route segments preserve their existing number to avoid gaps when chaining tramos. Useful for utility inventories (poles, luminaires, valves, manholes) where the numbering must follow the physical route rather than the feature ID order. Requirements: the points layer and the line layer must share a CRS suitable for distance calculation (geographic or projected). No external Python dependencies. Differences from similar tools: unlike attribute-based sorting or fid-based numbering, this plugin uses lineLocatePoint to project each point onto the line and sort by along-line distance, which correctly handles curved routes and points added out of capture order.
plugins.author: Dheiby Paz

plugins.name: Smart AutoSave
plugins.description: Auto-saves project on timer (20 min), layer add, and symbology change
plugins.about: Saves the current QGIS project automatically every 20 minutes, whenever a new layer is added, and whenever layer symbology changes. Works globally for any project without per-project configuration.
plugins.author: Thana Chirapiwat

plugins.name: GCN-HSI
plugins.description: Semi-automated Great Crested Newt Habitat Suitability Index (HSI) calculator. Created from improvements made to Oldham's (2000) original scoring system.
plugins.about:
Calculates the Great Crested Newt (GCN) Habitat Suitability Index for up to 10 candidate ponds per run. 
Now contains two tools. Remote Assessment tool automates SI1 - SI6 scoring (designed for fast pre-screening only). Full assessment requires field survey data. Supports per pond override to automated variables if field data is available. Includes road barrier detection to exclude habitats and ponds on far side of a road. Output is a polygon layer with per pond HSI scoring and traffic light symbology. Hope it helps.
plugins.author: Ciaran Egan

plugins.name: QWorkspaceSwitcher
plugins.description:
Create, manage and apply named QGIS interface
configurations (workspaces). Switch between different
working environments in one click from the toolbar.
plugins.about:
QWorkspace Switcher allows QGIS users to create, save
and apply named interface configurations called workspaces.
Each workspace defines which panels (QDockWidget), toolbars
(QToolBar) and menus are visible, and how they are organized
in the QGIS main window.

Key features:
- Create workspaces by capturing the current QGIS interface
- Apply a workspace in one click from the toolbar
- Configure button style (text, icon, icon+text, text+icon)
- Assign a custom icon to each workspace
- Add dropdown menus from other plugins per workspace
- Show or hide the QGIS menu bar per workspace
- Declarative .psp.json system for third-party plugins
- Blacklist system for deleted plugin workspaces
- Export/import workspace configuration file
- Emergency shortcut Ctrl+Shift+M to restore menu bar

Originally developed at CNR (Compagnie Nationale du Rhône)
for hydraulic modeling workflows. Designed as a generic,
domain-independent tool for any QGIS user or organization.
plugins.author: Adnan Benaboud — Compagnie Nationale du Rhône (CNR)

plugins.name: RasterPixelInfo
plugins.description: Displays row index, column index, and pixel values directly on the map canvas for every visible raster pixel. Includes multi-layer comparison panel and pixel border overlay.
plugins.about: This plugin shows raster pixel row/column indices and band values as canvas labels when zoomed in. A dockable panel shows real-time pixel info and a multi-layer comparison table. Labels, values, and pixel borders are independent and togglable. Works with any raster format supported by QGIS and handles CRS differences between the raster and the map canvas automatically.
plugins.author: Khalil

plugins.name: QGIS2Blender
plugins.description: This plugin prepares DEMs for use in Blender.
plugins.about: QGIS2Blender prepares DEM rasters for Blender heightmap workflows. It can mosaic multiple DEMs with a VRT, reproject to a target CRS, optionally clip by polygon AOI, fill NoData pixels before scaling, and export a UInt16 GeoTIFF scaled to 0-65535. No external Python dependencies are required.
plugins.author: Ben Leamon

plugins.name: ParcelFlux
plugins.description: Subdivide zoning blocks into parcels with minimum-frontage, depth and corner rules, width variation, row asymmetry, fishbone offset, and automatic residual merging.
plugins.about: ParcelFlux automates the subdivision of zoning blocks into parcels with natural variation. It supports single/double-row detection, minimum street frontage, explicit front-row depth and corner-plot widening, row-width asymmetry for differentiated front/rear facades, fishbone-style organic boundary offsets, H-line shift for asymmetric depth, and 3-pass automatic merging of residual fragments. Output is complete by construction: parcels that exceed the maximum area are split further, and anything still outside the envelope is kept and flagged rather than deleted, with a coverage report after every run. Results can be previewed before they are added, and four seeded layouts can be compared side by side. Developed at Dokuz Eylul University, Department of City and Regional Planning. Online User Manual & Documentation: https://yusufeminoglu.github.io/parcelflux/ | If you find this plugin helpful, please consider starring the repository on GitHub (https://github.com/YusufEminoglu/parcelflux)!
plugins.author: Yusuf Eminoglu

plugins.name: Minera Indices
plugins.description: Estimate mineral spectral indices from ASTER, Landsat (5/7/8/9), and Sentinel-2 satellite data. Auto-detects sensor type from input folder and exports all common indices as separate GeoTIFF files.
plugins.about: Minera Indices automatically detects your satellite sensor (ASTER, Landsat 5, 7, 8, 9, or Sentinel-2) from a selected folder of imagery and computes all applicable mineral spectral indices. Outputs include Iron Oxide, Ferrous Minerals, Clay Minerals, Alunite, Kaolinite, Carbonate, Gossan, Silica, and vegetation indices - each saved as an individual GeoTIFF.
plugins.author: Hatim

plugins.name: Smart OBIA
plugins.description: Plugin para Object-Based Image Analysis (OBIA) com Classificação ML (Random Forest, SVM, CatBoost), Segmentação e Índices RGB.
plugins.about: Plugin Smart OBIA para processamento avançado de imagens com segmentação e classificação de Machine Learning.
plugins.author: Leandro da Silva Gregorio

plugins.name: EquiMap Spatial Inequality Intelligence
plugins.description: EquiMap Spatial Inequality Intelligence is a QGIS plugin designed to generate spatial inequality diagnostics from two numeric polygon variables through bivariate mapping, inequality metrics, spatial autocorrelation analysis, and modern visual reporting.
plugins.about: EquiMap provides an integrated spatial inequality intelligence framework for QGIS. It combines bivariate choropleth mapping, Gini Index, Theil T Index, Hoover Index, Lorenz curve, concentration curve, Pearson and Spearman correlation, Global Moran I, Local Moran or LISA, Bivariate Moran, and Bivariate Local Moran or BiLISA. The recommended logic is directional: Variable Y represents demand, need, pressure, risk, exposure, or vulnerability, while Variable X represents service, supply, access, infrastructure, capacity, support, or resilience. Outputs include a classified spatial layer, QML style file, bivariate poster map, legend PNG, Lorenz curve PNG, concentration curve PNG, Moran scatterplot PNG, Bivariate Moran scatterplot PNG, LISA map PNG, BiLISA map PNG, summary dashboard PNG, summary CSV, priority ranking CSV, and automated HTML spatial inequality report.
plugins.author: Firman Afrianto, Maya Safira

plugins.name: GeoLogic Flight Planner
plugins.description: Generates high-efficiency flight routes with terrain following, compatible with the UAV.COM API (DJI Fly).
plugins.about: The GeoLogic Flight Planner is a professional-grade QGIS plugin designed for efficient drone mapping and aerial photogrammetry. It integrates spatial analysis with drone kinematics to generate high-efficiency flight paths that automatically adapt to terrain via Digital Elevation Models (DEMs). The plugin bridges the gap between GIS and field operations by translating complex mapping logic into native DJI WPML-compliant KMZ missions. Key features include intelligent waypoint densification to safeguard controller memory, kinematic-based flight time estimation for enhanced safety, and advanced route optimization that minimizes battery consumption and flight time. Built to provide an autonomous, transparent, and robust alternative to proprietary software, it empowers field professionals to plan and execute precise missions directly from their GIS workspace.
plugins.author: Victor Moreira Naves Ribeiro

plugins.name: gmqr
plugins.description: Generate Google Maps URLs and QR codes from clicked map locations
plugins.about: Generate Google Maps URLs and QR codes from clicked locations on the QGIS map canvas. Useful for field surveys, mobile sharing, and location guidance.
plugins.author: Rei Ito

plugins.name: Water Masking Plugin
plugins.description: A comprehensive tool for extracting water masks and generating smoothed waterbody polygons from multispectral satellite imagery.
plugins.about:
Water Masking Plugin is a specialized QGIS toolkit designed to extract accurate water masks and generate smoothed waterbody polygons from multispectral satellite imagery.

Core Workflow:
1-Indices Calculation: Calculates NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index), MNDWI (Modified Normalized     Difference Water Index), and NWI (New Water Index).
2-Water Masking Equation: Uses the equation (MNDWI > 0) AND (NWI > 0) AND (NDVI < 0.1) to extract the water mask.
3-Noise Removal: Applies a sieve filter to remove isolated noise pixels.
4-Geometry Smoothing: Rounds the sharp stair-step edges of the final polygon.
plugins.author: Mohamed Aly Nasef

plugins.name: Rosa dos Ventos Geomagnética (Magnetic Declination)
plugins.description: Generates an interactive compass rose demonstrating the magnetic declination of the day based on the WMM-2025 model. Exports to SVG/PNG and adds it as a vector layer.
plugins.about: Plugin created by Alessandro Pimentel - Phone: +55 (91) 98505-6742. This plugin calculates the magnetic declination of any location on the globe for the current date using the World Magnetic Model (WMM-2025). It displays a stylized and professional compass rose in real-time, allowing export to SVG/PNG and insertion of the geometry as a layer in the map.
plugins.author: Alessandro Pimentel

plugins.name: PlanX Urban Procedural 3D
plugins.description: Parametric 3D urban design and procedural planning toolbox with real-time compliance feedback.
plugins.about: PlanX Urban Procedural 3D is an interactive parametric design tool for QGIS. It enables planners to select parcel/block boundaries, open a local Three.js 3D editor, adjust setbacks, building heights, and typologies live in the browser, and sync the generated geometry and compliance metrics back into the QGIS project. Developed with feedback from educational workflows at Dokuz Eylul University, Department of City and Regional Planning. Online User Manual & Documentation: https://yusufeminoglu.github.io/planx_urban_procedural_3d/ | If you find this plugin helpful, please consider starring the repository on GitHub (https://github.com/YusufEminoglu/planx_urban_procedural_3d)!
plugins.author: Yusuf Eminoglu

plugins.name: GIS Layer Converter
plugins.description: Advanced schema-union vector layer converter, name-collision protector, and database compiler tool.
plugins.about: Safely exports vector datasets with custom attribute unions, protected duplicate-name suffixing alignments, embedded GeoPackage styling, and structured HTML popup generation for Google Earth KML outputs.
plugins.author: Onkar Keskar

plugins.name: CRS Mismatch Detector
plugins.description: Scans your QGIS project for layers whose CRS differs from the project CRS and offers safe reprojection by creating new output layers.
plugins.about: CRS Mismatch Detector checks whether the layers in your QGIS project use the same CRS as the project CRS. If a layer uses a different CRS, the plugin marks it as a mismatch and lets you create a corrected reprojected copy. The original layer is never modified.
plugins.author: Karthik

plugins.name: Building ACR
plugins.description: A QGIS-based plugin for calculating building- and climate-specific hourly Air Change Rates (ACR) at urban scale, integrating wind speed correction and the 3ZLPM model for improved infiltration modelling in UBEM applications.
plugins.about: This plugin computes hourly building- and climate-specific Air Change Rates (ACR) to improve infiltration modelling in Urban Building Energy Modelling (UBEM). It integrates wind speed corrections at facade level using urban canyon algorithms, outdoor temperature correction via the Urban Weather Generator (UWG/UMEP), and hourly ACR simulation using a Three-Zone Lumped Parameter Model (3ZLPM) or CONTAM. Inputs include building geometry, air permeability, roughness length, and hourly weather data.
plugins.author: Yasemin Usta; Xuan Zhou; Guglielmina Mutani

plugins.name: Universal XY Converter
plugins.description: Universal coordinate converter supporting all QGIS CRS (200+ systems) with native BFTM support for Burkina Faso. Convert between any CRS: WGS84, UTM zones 1-60, Adindan, Clarke 1880, NAD83, ETRS89, GDA2020, and custom PROJ strings. Features: single conversion, batch CSV processing, interactive map picking, support for DD, DMS (with French notations O/E/N/S), and meters.
plugins.about: Universal XY Converter is a powerful QGIS plugin for coordinate conversion between any Coordinate Reference Systems (CRS) available in QGIS, with native support for BFTM (Burkina Faso Transverse Mercator). Features: single conversion, batch CSV processing, interactive map picking, support for DD, DMS (with French notations O for Ouest, E for Est, N for Nord, S for Sud), and meters format. Now supports Clarke 1880 and Adindan in degrees and UTM zones (all zones 1-60 N/S) with region-specific parameters: West Africa (-118,-14,218) and Cameroon (-166,-15,204). Multilingual support: French/English automatically based on QGIS language.
plugins.author: Bazikité Jean-Baptiste KIBORA | GIS Developer

plugins.name: 3D OSM Model
plugins.description: Create a styled OSM map and procedural 3D city, then export publication-ready images, PDF, SVG, HTML, or video.
plugins.about: 3D OSM Model is a fast, single-button companion to PlanX 3D City. Select a small area (up to ~300 ha), and the plugin downloads OpenStreetMap buildings, roads, cycleways, waterways, lakes and ponds, greens, car parks, pedestrian squares, trees and street furniture (bus stops, benches, lamps, bins) using their native OSM tags, builds the study boundary as the shape you choose - inscribed circle, rounded rectangle, rectangle or the exact selected polygon (the model base extends 5 m beyond it with softly rounded corners), and opens an interactive, English-only Three.js 3D city viewer. A coordinated "Map & web theme" picker styles both the native QGIS layer group and the exported city, with Editorial Paper active by default plus the existing calm and stylised palettes. Native layers arrive categorized by building/ground function, roads use hierarchy-aware metric widths, and water, trees and furniture have coordinated cartographic symbols. A single click adds the live OpenStreetMap tile layer to your project so an empty map can be navigated and framed before exporting, and that same layer is offered as the ground underlay. A basemap layer (raster, satellite/XYZ tiles or vector) can optionally be draped under the city and restyled live - opacity, blend mode, brightness, contrast, saturation and tint - in the viewer's Basemap and Texture panel; procedural kerb sidewalks line both sides of every street. Roads, sidewalks and bike lanes are drawn procedurally with lane markings; pedestrians keep to the sidewalks and cars to the carriageway; parks, woods and forests are planted with procedural trees so green areas read as wooded rather than flat; buildings are coloured by OSM function - with a subtle per-building shade variation so blocks read as many individual buildings - and default to a function-aware floor count when no level data exists. Pyramid, hip, gable, shed and flat roof controls are supported, including standard OSM roof-shape tags. An external DEM can optionally be added. Built on the PlanX 3D City viewer engine at Dokuz Eylul University, Department of City and Regional Planning. Online User Manual & Documentation: https://yusufeminoglu.github.io/osm_3d_model/ | If you find this plugin helpful, please consider starring the repository on GitHub (https://github.com/YusufEminoglu/osm_3d_model)!
plugins.author: Yusuf Eminoglu

plugins.name: Polygon validator EUDR 2
plugins.description: EUDR-oriented polygon quality-control suite: geometry repair and overlap cleaning, interior centroids with Longitude/Latitude, self-intersection repair with hole filling and Field_ID deduplication, and cross-layer overlap marking. Redesigned modern interface.
plugins.about: Polygon validator EUDR 2 is a quality-control suite for land, cadastral, agricultural and forestry data under EUDR workflows. Four tools, a redesigned interface and a Processing algorithm. (1) Validator: repairs geometries (makeValid, duplicate-node removal, buffer 0, QGIS-internal validation), removes overlaps above a business threshold (18 percent by default) keeping the most reliable polygon, removes exact duplicates, full containments, tiny areas and slivers to a deleted layer, and annotates partial overlaps. (2) Centroids: generates a points layer whose points are guaranteed inside each polygon (point on surface), with computed Longitude and Latitude (WGS84). (3) Self-intersection: repairs self-intersections, multipart to singlepart, computes Surface_Ha, removes tiny areas, fills interior holes created by repair, and deduplicates Field_ID codes. (4) EUDR platform: detects overlaps between two layers and marks/selects the overlapping features in both attribute tables above a threshold, without creating any output file. Deforestation detection and its compliance dashboard are now provided by the separate standalone plugin "Deforestation check".
plugins.author: Jean David Konan

plugins.name: Self-intersection by JDK
plugins.description: Repairs self-intersections, converts multipart to singlepart, computes area (Surface_Ha) and removes polygons from 0 to 0.25 ha.
plugins.about: Self-intersection by JDK repairs geometries (makeValid + buffer 0 to remove self-intersections), applies "Multipart to singleparts" to isolate non-conforming geometries, creates a Surface_Ha = $area / 10000 field, then removes features whose 0 <= Surface_Ha < 0.25 ha (upper bound excluded), producing a deleted-polygons layer. Graphical interface plus a Processing algorithm (Model designer / batch / qgis_process). Designed for geometric quality control (land, cadastre, agriculture, forestry, EUDR/RA).
plugins.author: JDK

plugins.name: GML to DXF (CityGML LoD2)
plugins.description: Converts CityGML LoD2 building files (e.g. from BayernAtlas) to DXF 3D faces for CAD use.
plugins.about: Batch-converts CityGML LoD2 .gml files to .dxf files containing 3D faces on a dedicated layer "LoD2_Gebaeude". Supports gml:posList and gml:pos coordinate encoding. Ideal for processing Bavarian building data from BayernAtlas / LfU.
plugins.author: Odysseas Deutsch

plugins.name: Otomatisasi D3TLH
plugins.description: Automated D3TLH analysis and environmental carrying capacity assessment tools for QGIS.
plugins.about: Otomatisasi D3TLH is a QGIS plugin developed to streamline and automate workflows for D3TLH (Environmental Carrying Capacity and Environmental Carrying Capability) assessments. The plugin integrates demographic, ecological, environmental, and spatial analysis models into a unified processing framework, reducing manual data preparation and calculation efforts. It provides tools for generating standardized outputs that support environmental planning, regional development assessment, and decision-making processes. The plugin was developed by the Directorate of Environmental Impact Prevention and Regional Sectoral Policy, Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Indonesia (KLH/BPLH), with support from Yayasan Lokus Bijak Hijau Lestari (LOKAHITA).
plugins.author: Fadillah Azhar Deaudin Kurniawan, Sitarani Safitri, Dini Aprilia Norvyani, Suchi Rahmadani, Fariz Rizaldy Wibowo

plugins.name: Summarizer
plugins.description: Summarizes QGIS layers and prepares charts, dashboards, and report-ready analytical outputs.
plugins.about: Summarizer helps analysts explore QGIS project layers, build attribute summaries, generate charts, prepare dashboard-ready tables, and export structured analytical results from geospatial data. Core workflows run locally inside QGIS and do not require external services.
plugins.author: Jeandson Marques

plugins.name: NPN Decoder
plugins.description: Sistema de Inteligencia Territorial y Auditoría Catastral para la deconstrucción, validación masiva del NPN (22/30 dígitos) e integración en tiempo real con la Ventanilla Única de Registro (VUR).
plugins.about: NPN Decoder es la solución empresarial definitiva para ingenieros catastrales, tasadores, desarrolladores inmobiliarios y gestores de infraestructura en Colombia. Este plugin automatiza la validación de calidad y deconstrucción analítica del Número Predial Nacional (NPN 22 y 30 dígitos) bajo estándares LADM-COL. Integra un potente motor de consulta bidireccional en tiempo real con la Ventanilla Única de Registro (VUR-SNR) para confrontar áreas elipsoidales calculadas en QGIS contra áreas jurídicas registradas en los folios de matrícula, alertando al instante sobre embargos, gravámenes y discrepancias espaciales críticas. Diseñado para optimizar los procesos de debida diligencia de tierras, control de calidad de bases de datos vectoriales catastrales y saneamiento predial con precisión analítica excepcional.
plugins.author: Albert Gaviria

plugins.name: GeoMark
plugins.description: Create named points, lines, polygons, rectangles, and circles on the map canvas with styling, coordinates, labels, and CSV import/export support.
plugins.about: GeoMark allows users to interactively create named Point, LineString, Polygon, Rectangle, and Circle features on the QGIS canvas. Features are automatically organized into shared GeoMark layers inside a dedicated GEOMARK group. Includes color styling, SVG markers, line width control, coordinate attributes (X/Y, DD, DMS), labeling, autocomplete history, usage tracking, and CSV import/export.
plugins.author: Achmad Amrulloh

plugins.name: HELIX Labelling Framework
plugins.description: Prepare robust vector and raster label workflows on a common reference grid, from class schemes and temporal alignment to context features, soft targets, uncertainty and QA reports.
plugins.about: HELIX Labelling Framework is a modular QGIS Processing toolbox for preparing heterogeneous vector and raster label sources as grid-aligned, time-aware, context-aware and uncertainty-aware supervision products. Documentation and a small synthetic test dataset are included in the docs folder and in the public repository README. Dependencies are QGIS/PyQGIS with GDAL and NumPy as provided by standard QGIS installations. The plugin is written in Python using the QGIS PyQt compatibility layer and is intended for Windows, Linux and macOS. Copyright (C) 2026 Sarah Hauser, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT).
plugins.author: Sarah Hauser (Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, KIT)

plugins.name: Network-Based Hierarchical Feature Augmentation
plugins.description: Augments road network features by aggregating attribute values from hierarchical BFS neighbourhood levels (L1, L2, ..., LN). Each field can have its own neighbourhood depth and aggregation method (mean, sum, min, max, median, std). L1_Count ... LN_Count columns are generated automatically.
plugins.about: Implements the Network-Based Hierarchical Feature Augmentation method (Hacar, Altafini & Cutini, ISPRS IJGI 2024, doi:10.3390/ijgi13120456). Select any number of numeric fields and configure per-field neighbourhood depth (N) and aggregation method independently. Available in both the Processing Toolbox (automatable) and as a dockable panel (interactive).
plugins.author: Müslüm Hacar

plugins.name: OSM Quick 3D
plugins.description: One-click OpenStreetMap into native QGIS: function-styled vector layers plus flat-roof 3D building massing on a selectable study-area shape (rectangle, rounded rectangle, circle, hexagon or your own selected polygon), with selectable map themes, an optional recessed base and a basemap underlay.
plugins.about: OSM Quick 3D is a fast, native companion to the browser-based 3D OSM Model plugin. Pick the visible map area (or the extent of your selected features) and a study-area shape — rectangle, rounded rectangle, circle, hexagon, or your own selected polygon — and the plugin downloads OpenStreetMap buildings, roads, cycleways, waterways, greens, trees and street furniture straight into QGIS as memory layers, already styled by function: buildings coloured by OSM use, roads by highway class and metric width, water blue, greens green. The buildings are then extruded with QGIS's own 3D symbology into a clean flat-roof massing model whose height comes from OSM (tagged height, else floor count, else a sensible default), so it shows directly in a QGIS 3D Map View with no browser and no web server. Building colours are selectable and applied identically in 2D and 3D: by OSM function, or a soft height-graduated tint (gray, warm, teal, salmon, purple or sand), with multiple map themes for different cartographic looks. An optional height-exaggeration factor makes low-rise districts read in the 3D view, and trees get a matching 3D pass as simple green canopies. The city stands on an optional recessed ground base (the study area buffered outward by 5 m, extruded as a plinth from 2 m below up to ground level), tinted to harmonise with the chosen building colours. Every downloaded layer lands inside one tidy layer-tree group, an optional basemap layer is moved under the city to act as the ground, and the whole result can optionally be saved to a single GeoPackage so it survives a project reload instead of vanishing as a memory layer. The Theme & Style dock controls the native 3D scene, including per-layer visibility in 3D without hiding those layers from the 2D map. Buildings and roads can optionally be labelled by their OSM name with a white halo. Each building also carries a computed footprint area and an estimated gross floor area (footprint times floors) as real columns, and the run reports the area totals, so the output is ready for quick planning quantities. Overpass responses are cached on disk for a week, so re-running on the same area opens instantly without hitting the rate-limited public API again. Because the output is plain native layers, it scales to far larger areas than a web 3D scene; the practical limit is the public Overpass API. Built at Dokuz Eylul University, Department of City and Regional Planning. Online User Manual & Documentation: https://yusufeminoglu.github.io/osm_quick_3d/ | If you find this plugin helpful, please consider starring the repository on GitHub (https://github.com/YusufEminoglu/osm_quick_3d)!
plugins.author: Yusuf Eminoglu

plugins.name: TairuDB
plugins.description: Connect QGIS to Tairu Maps (https://tairumaps.com) for two-way cloud sync, editable field records, and offline .tairudb map generation.
plugins.about: TairuDB adds a Tairu Maps dock to QGIS for field-mapping workflows. Sign in with your Tairu Maps account using e-mail, Google, or Apple, browse your maps, and exchange data in both directions: pull app records into editable GeoPackage layers, download TairuDB files as raster layers, push vector layers back as records with a diff preview, and generate and upload offline .tairudb rasters for a selected area. The classic Processing algorithm (Tairu > TairuDB) and the GeoPDF converter remain available for local exports. Cloud sync requires an Online or Real-time Tairu Maps plan.
plugins.author: Daniel Hulshof Saint Martin

plugins.name: Geometry Calc
plugins.description: Calculate area, length, and buffer for vector layers as per the user input.
plugins.about: A QGIS plugin to calculate area, length, and buffers for vector layers.
plugins.author: Kunal Dharod

plugins.name: Stereoplot
plugins.description: Interactive stereographic projection plotting and analysis tool for QGIS
plugins.about: Displays geologic structural data on equal-area stereonets and rose diagrams. Supports automatic structural data-type detection, density contouring, best-fit girdles, bearing-plane visualisation, kinematic arrows, attribute-based classification, category styling, dynamic filtering using QGIS expressions, and interactive category visibility controls.
plugins.author: Julien Perret (UWA-CET) & Mark Jessell (UWA-CET)

plugins.name: beaconGIS — Building Damage Assessment
plugins.description: AI building-level damage classification from pre/post-disaster RGB imagery, using a Siamese U-Net ensemble running on ONNX Runtime.
plugins.about: Classifies buildings into No Damage, Minor, Major, or Destroyed using a two-network deep-learning pipeline (LocalizationUNet + SiameseUNet, SeResNeXt-50 (32x4d) encoder, two-model ensemble) trained on the full public xView2/xBD dataset with Inria Aerial Image Labeling pretraining. xView2 official scorer Combined F1 = 0.7312. Designed for disaster-response teams: includes AOI clipping, CPU Fast Mode for non-GPU machines, automatic CRS-aware pre/post alignment, GSD normalization, offline template-driven SitRep generator (no LLM API), GeoPackage / GeoTIFF mask / JSON sidecar export. Runs entirely on ONNX Runtime (no PyTorch install required). Model weights (~234 MB fp16, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) are downloaded on first use from the plugin's GitHub release page over plain HTTPS with SHA-256 verification — no account or token required. Outputs are draft assessments for human review — not authoritative ground truth.
plugins.author: Adem Özel

plugins.name: AgenticGIS
plugins.description: An in-QGIS agentic chat assistant that operates QGIS via PyQGIS. Connect with an API key, compatible endpoint, or local CLI agent.
plugins.about: AgenticGIS adds a chat dock to QGIS. Type a request in natural language and an LLM agent carries it out by generating and running PyQGIS code, giving it access to QGIS, Processing, project layers, and installed plugins. Requirements: QGIS 3.22 or newer (including QGIS 4) and an LLM connection using a provider API key, compatible custom endpoint, or installed local CLI agent. The plugin has no bundled Python package dependencies. Google Earth Engine features are optional and require the Google Earth Engine QGIS plugin to be installed and authenticated separately.
plugins.author: Muhammad Alichamdan

plugins.name: InSAR Earthquake Modelling
plugins.description: The plugin helps in forward modelling to help us visualize the structural geology(strike/dip/rake/depth etc.)of earthquake's slip from the wrapped interferograms.
plugins.about: The plugin is created in python script and follows the Okada model(1985) for fault forward modelling.
plugins.author: Daksh17440

plugins.name: Topology Checker Pro
plugins.description: Detect, visualise & fix vector topology errors — with canvas markers, zoom-to-error, and step-by-step fix guidance
plugins.about:
Topology Checker Pro scans any vector layer for geometry errors
(null geometry, invalid geometry, self-intersections, duplicates,
overlaps, gaps, dangles, multipart features) and displays the results
in a clean docked panel.

Key features:
• Colour-coded markers drawn directly on the map canvas for every error
• Click any error row to zoom to it and see a bright yellow highlight
• Full-feature orange outline shows exactly which polygon/line is affected
• Solution panel: plain-English explanation + numbered manual fix steps
• One-click Auto-Fix for Invalid Geometry, Self-Intersections and Multipart
• Prev / Next navigation through all errors
• Export results to CSV
• Works with QGIS 3.x (Qt5/PyQt5) and QGIS 4.x (Qt6/PyQt6)
plugins.author: Cyanide

plugins.name: Raster Clipper
plugins.description: Clip raster layers by vector mask with All-Touched boundary control and detailed pixel statistics.
plugins.about:
Raster Clipper lets you clip any raster layer using a vector boundary (SHP, GPKG, or any
loaded vector layer) with fine-grained pixel-inclusion control.

Key features:
• All Touched mode — include every pixel that even touches the boundary,
not just pixels whose centre falls inside (uses GDAL CUTLINE_ALL_TOUCHED).
• Temporary file support — clip directly to an auto-generated temp path;
no need to choose an output file for quick exploratory work.
• Detailed pixel statistics — WIDTH_IN_PIXELS, HEIGHT_IN_PIXELS,
TOTAL_PIXEL_COUNT, NODATA_PIXEL_COUNT, and VALID_PIXEL_COUNT per band,
displayed in a styled dark terminal panel after every clip.
• Auto-loads the clipped result into the QGIS canvas.
• GeoPackage-aware — correctly resolves |layername= source paths.
• Robust nodata detection — handles float NaN, integer overflow, and
cases where GDAL does not write nodata metadata to the output file.

Built with pure GDAL (gdal.WarpOptions) for maximum compatibility.
plugins.author: Cyanide

plugins.name: CityLume Planner NTL Based Urban Structure and Planning Intelligence
plugins.description:
CityLume Planner is a QGIS plugin for analyzing nighttime light dynamics, urban structure, planning mismatch, future urban centers, and spatial planning action priorities using NTL time series, POI, building, road, population, and spatial plan allocation data.

The plugin transforms multi year NTL and supporting spatial datasets into urban dynamics classes, future core probability, shrinking risk, center hierarchy, planning mismatch typologies, and action matrix recommendations for evidence based urban and regional planning.
plugins.about:
CityLume Planner provides an integrated spatial planning intelligence framework for diagnosing urban growth, decline, center hierarchy, and planning mismatch using nighttime light time series and complementary urban datasets.

It combines NTL trend analysis, POI and building aggregation, road accessibility, optional population raster, optional spatial plan allocation, and optional planned center data to produce interpretable planning indicators and recommendations.

Outputs include an analysis grid, future core candidates, CSV and XLSX summaries, modern PNG maps and charts, GIF animations, metadata JSON, and an automatic diagnostic TXT report.

CityLume Planner is designed for urban structure evaluation, spatial plan monitoring, future service center detection, growth control analysis, urban regeneration diagnostics, and evidence based planning policy support.
plugins.author: Firman Afrianto, Maya Safira

plugins.name: DEM Route Profile and Terrain Cost Analyzer
plugins.description: DEM route profile, 3D terrain section, multi-DEM comparison, terrain cost analysis, and basic earthwork cut/fill volume tool.
plugins.about: This plugin creates terrain profiles from clicked route points on DEM raster layers. It supports 2D elevation profiles, 3D section viewing, multi-DEM comparison, elevation difference charts, slope-based terrain cost calculation, basic earthwork cut/fill volume analysis from DEM and selected polygon, CSV export, GeoPackage sample point export, 3D LineStringZ export, and project CRS information.
plugins.author: CarbonAce Co., Ltd.

plugins.name: Plugin Hub
plugins.description: A central launcher to discover, search, and open all your installed QGIS plugins from one dock panel.
plugins.about: Plugin Hub is an all-in-one plugin management center for QGIS. It lets you search, install, launch, update, and uninstall plugins from a single dockable interface, eliminating the need to navigate multiple menus and toolbars. Features include instant plugin search, one-click launch, drag-to-reorder favorites pinning, manual category overrides, an archive section for plugins you want out of the way, recent plugin history, category filtering, automatic rescanning after installs/uninstalls, installed plugin management, direct uninstall support, and a clean, organized workspace for faster access to your tools.
plugins.author: Shyam Mishra

plugins.name: NextGIS Toolbox
plugins.description: NextGIS Toolbox provider for QGIS
plugins.about: NextGIS Toolbox provider for QGIS. Sends tasks to NextGIS Toolbox server and recieve results. Developed by NextGIS. Any feedback is welcome at https://nextgis.com/contact. See more on https://toolbox.nextgis.com/
plugins.author: NextGIS

plugins.name: RSRP Cumulative Analyzer
plugins.description: Calculate before and after RSRP CSV sample percentages and cumulative percentages by RSRP range.
plugins.about: RSRP Cumulative Analyzer compares two element tile RSRP CSV files, Before and After, then summarizes sample count, percentage, and cumulative percentage for standard RSRP ranges.
plugins.author: Taufik Andrian

plugins.name: IGM Verto Coordinate Converter
plugins.description: Coordinate conversion using the official IGM grids (Verto online API) - Conversione coordinate con i grigliati ufficiali IGM (API Verto online).
plugins.about: Plugin for QGIS 3 and 4 that converts coordinates using the IGM "Verto online" REST API (official Italian national grids), more accurate than standard PROJ transformations between Italian datums (Monte Mario/Roma40, ED50, IGM95, ETRS89/RDN2008). Features: reproject vector layers, manual coordinate conversion, batch conversion from CSV, map-click tool and a Processing algorithm. Requires an internet connection. --- Plugin per QGIS 3 e 4 che converte coordinate usando l'API REST "Verto online" dell'IGM (grigliati nazionali ufficiali), piu' precisa delle trasformazioni PROJ standard tra i datum italiani (Monte Mario/Roma40, ED50, IGM95, ETRS89/RDN2008). Funzioni: riproiezione di layer vettoriali, conversione manuale, conversione batch da CSV, strumento di click sulla mappa e algoritmo Processing. Richiede una connessione internet. Servizio IGM: https://igmi.esercito.difesa.it/servizi/verto-online/
plugins.author: Federico Gianoli

plugins.name: QGIS AI Assistant
plugins.description: AI-powered spatial queries inside QGIS
plugins.about: QGIS AI Agent is an AI-powered plugin that lets you query and analyze your GIS data using natural language. Simply type what you want to do and the AI agent will execute the spatial operations automatically. Powered by OpenRouter API (supports free Kimi K2 model). No expensive API keys required — get a free key at openrouter.ai
plugins.author: kodeezabdullah

plugins.name: Solar Site Suitability (AHP)
plugins.description: Multi-criteria (AHP) site suitability analysis for utility-scale solar PV farms, from DEM, manual GHI or ERA5 SSRD, and land cover. Region-agnostic.
plugins.about: Solar Site Suitability (AHP) identifies suitable areas for utility-scale photovoltaic solar farms using a spatial Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis based on the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP, Saaty 1980). Starting from a DEM, a land-cover raster, and either a manual GHI raster or ERA5 SSRD downloaded from Copernicus, it derives slope and aspect, reclassifies each criterion to a 1-5 suitability scale, combines them with AHP weights (validated by the Consistency Ratio CR < 0.10), applies boolean exclusion masks (steep slope, pole-facing aspect, protected/urban/water land cover) and extracts contiguous viable polygons above a minimum area. The tool is region-agnostic: thresholds, break values, land-cover classes, AHP weights, minimum area and the favourable orientation (hemisphere selector) are all user-defined, so it works anywhere in the world, not only in Colombia. Dependencies: standard QGIS 3.28+ plus optional cdsapi in the QGIS Python environment for the ERA5 download workflow. Outputs: suitability rasters, viable-sites GeoPackage, ERA5 request/NetCDF/GeoTIFF/CSV products, and HTML/CSV reports.
plugins.author: Fernan Jose Severich Diaz, Pedro Joaquin Perilla Vargas

plugins.name: SedonaDB Tools
plugins.description: High-performance out-of-core spatial operations powered by SedonaDB. Includes Spatial Clip, Spatial Join (Join Attributes by Location), and a dependency installer.
plugins.about: SedonaDB Spatial Tools provides QGIS Processing algorithms that leverage SedonaDB for large-scale, out-of-core spatial operations. All tools operate on GeoPackage layers and stream results directly to disk. Includes: Spatial Clip, Spatial Join (Join Attributes by Location), and an OSGeo4W-based dependency installer for sedona and pyogrio.
plugins.author: Pradip

plugins.name: Rename Field and type
plugins.description: This plugin let user changes the field's name and field type from a vector layer
plugins.about: First, the user select a vector layer from vector layers list. Next, he select a field from selected layer and select the field type. Then, user enter field's new name. Finally, he must push rename button.
plugins.author: Anustup Jana

plugins.description: IT: Client non ufficiale per le API IGM: conversione di coordinate e layer vettoriali tra datum italiani. / EN: Unofficial client for the IGM API: coordinate and vector layer conversion between Italian datums.
plugins.about: IT: GeoBridge e' un client QGIS non ufficiale. Il codice del plugin e' distribuito sotto licenza GPL-2.0-or-later.
